title: Union of records: the first branch sharing any field name wins and the rest of the data is dropped
rationale: The reconstructor selects a RECORD branch if ANY of the node children match ANY field name of that branch, then commits to it. When two branches share a field the earlier branch always wins, and the losing branch exclusive fields are dropped without error. Giving the wrong branch a nullable field with a default guarantees it builds successfully, so the rescue path never fires.
catchesBugClass: Union branch resolution by first-partial-match with no completeness check. Correct behaviour would score branches by how many children they consume and how many they orphan.
cannotCatch: Cannot catch the disjoint-field-names case, which works correctly today and should be added as its own control. It also cannot catch a union of two records with IDENTICAL field sets, which is information-theoretically unresolvable from the flattened form.

predicted.detail: The wrong branch is selected and two children go unconsumed. Total silence: no exception, and a structurally valid record of the wrong type.

measurementNote: CONFIRMED, PLUS A NEW FINDING THE PREDICTION MISSED. The wrong branch is selected exactly as traced and routing/account are dropped. But the losing branch's defaulted field does not come back as a Java null: it comes back as org.apache.avro.JsonProperties.NULL_VALUE, a singleton OBJECT. Any consumer testing `value == null` on a defaulted nullable field sees a non-null object of an Avro-internal type. The corpus renders it as AVRO_NULL_DEFAULT so the distinction is visible and so the fixture does not depend on an identity hash code. Filed as a new defect for triage: useSchemaDefaults should materialise Avro's null default as a real null.
